skill.name: lint-typecheck
skill.description: Run ESLint and TypeScript type checking on the frontend codebase. Use when user mentions "lint", "type check", "check code", "eslint", "tsc", or before committing changes.
skill.summary: Run frontend ESLint and TypeScript checks, then report lint and type errors before code review.
skill.author: AppleLamps

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline command formatting in SKILL.md. The skill uses fixed frontend lint and type-check commands, and it requires confirmation before auto-fixes. No prompt injection, credential access, network behavior, or data exfiltration intent was found.

content.user_title: Run Frontend Lint and Type Checks
content.value_statement: Frontend changes can hide lint and type errors before review. This skill runs ESLint and TypeScript checks and reports actionable results.
actual_capabilities: Runs the configured frontend lint workflow when requested.
Runs a TypeScript compilation check without emitting build output.
Reports lint warnings, lint errors, and type errors in one summary.
Lists detected issues with file locations for review.
Offers ESLint auto-fixes only after user confirmation.
limitations: Requires a frontend directory with npm-based lint and TypeScript tooling.
Does not automatically fix TypeScript errors.
Does not change TypeScript configuration to suppress failures.
May execute project-defined npm tooling when checks are requested.

use_cases.title: Validate Frontend Changes
use_cases.description: Run lint and type checks before opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Review Contributor Work
use_cases.description: Check whether submitted frontend changes pass the project quality gates.

use_cases.title: Verify AI-Generated Code
use_cases.description: Confirm that generated UI changes pass lint and TypeScript checks.

prompt_templates.title: Run Basic Lint
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check after small frontend edits.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the frontend lint check and summarize any warnings or errors.

prompt_templates.title: Check Types Too
prompt_templates.prompt: Run frontend lint and TypeScript checks. Group the results by tool and include file locations.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare For Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Run lint first, then run the TypeScript no-emit check. If ESLint can auto-fix issues, ask before applying fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Triage Failures
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced diagnosis when several checks fail.
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate this branch before commit. Triage lint and type failures by likely cause, then recommend the smallest safe fixes.

output_examples.output: Lint completed with two warnings and no errors. Type checking was not requested for this run.

output_examples.input: Check for type errors before commit.
output_examples.output: Type checking found one mismatch in the profile form. The issue appears related to a nullable value.
Lint passed with no warnings. Type checking passed, so the frontend quality checks are clean.

best_practices: Run the checks before committing frontend changes.
Review the reported issues before approving any auto-fixes.
Keep configuration changes separate from normal lint and type fixes.
anti_patterns: Using the skill to hide errors by changing TypeScript configuration.
Applying ESLint auto-fixes without reviewing the proposed action.
Running the skill in projects without the expected frontend npm setup.

faq.question: What does this skill check?
faq.answer: It checks frontend ESLint results and TypeScript compilation status.

faq.question: Does it change files?
faq.answer: It starts with read-only checks. ESLint fixes require user confirmation.

faq.question: Can it fix TypeScript errors?
faq.answer: It identifies type mismatches and can recommend fixes, but it does not automatically repair them.

faq.question: What project structure does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects a frontend directory with npm lint and TypeScript tooling.

faq.question: Can I use it before a commit?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed to validate frontend changes before commit or review.

faq.question: Is it intended for backend checks?
faq.answer: No. The instructions target the frontend codebase only.
